result.title: Physical regime changes expose formula misuse in large language models
result.comment: 19 pages, 9 figures, 1 table; Supplementary Information appended. Code and data: https://github.com/acodercat/AtmosRegime
result.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly employed for scientific computing across the Earth and environmental sciences, but problems in these fields often involve distinct physical regimes. LLMs may fail to recognize these regime-dependent constraints, applying formulas outside their domains of validity and producing plausible but physically incorrect results. We systematically investigate these failures through controlled experiments and assess whether post-training can improve regime-aware reasoning. Across 72 physical mechanisms, we find frontier LLMs frequently misapply formulas outside their regimes of validity, reducing accuracy by 13-57 percentage points. Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards enables Qwen3.5-9B to match DeepSeek V4 Flash (284B) on regime-dependent tasks, but its effectiveness is limited by the formulas available in the base model. Combining supervised fine-tuning on a few worked examples with reinforcement learning improves accuracy by 61 percentage points, while distillation from a teacher supplied with the correct formula raises accuracy from 0% to 71%.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在 72 种物理机制上考察 LLM 是否会把公式用到有效范围之外，并比较 RLVR、少量示例 SFT 加 RL、以及由教师提供正确公式的蒸馏等训练后手段能否改善这种「区分物理适用区间」的推理。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽属纯文本科学计算且不涉及 latent 或视觉，但其「适用条件是否被保留并真正用于答案」的诊断，以及用教师给出的正确中间公式监督、可验证奖励训练的线索，可供核查 LVR 中轨迹监督与贡献分配问题。
